why:
phase-381 W3/W4. Same verb as ROS 2; the RECEIVER differs. ROS 2 hangs the graph off a node because each Node/Context owns a participant; a nano-ros image opens ONE session for the whole image -- a session per node is RAM a 128 KiB target does not have -- and the Executor owns it. NOT a `rename`: the name follows the receiver, and the receiver is where the session is. The SUBSCRIBER/SUBSCRIPTION word is chosen per language from that language's own upstream, which is why the three differ on purpose: rcl says `subscriber`, rclcpp and rclrs say `subscription`, and the vtable slot says `subscriber` because upstream rmw does (RFC-0054). rclcpp has no `*_by_node` form for subscriptions at all, so its WORD comes from its vocabulary (`create_subscription`, `Subscription<T>`) rather than from a method it lacks. Recorded so this does not read as the drift issue 0788 collects -- 0788 is about our languages disagreeing with NO rule; here the rule is 'follow your own upstream'.

phase-428 W5 (2026-09-06) — ledgering a recorded sweep finding. W3 F16. THE REASON ABOVE CONTAINS A FALSE CLAIM and it is the more valuable half of this correction.

The sentence "rclcpp has no `*_by_node` form for subscriptions at all, so the WORD comes from its vocabulary rather than from a method it lacks" is wrong. The form EXISTS upstream, spelled `get_subscriber_names_and_types_by_node`, on `rclcpp::node_interfaces::NodeGraphInterface` — beside `get_publisher_...`, `get_service_...` and `get_client_...`. What is narrowly true is that `rclcpp::Node` itself re-exposes only the SERVICE form; the other three are reached through `node->get_node_graph_interface()`.

So the SUBSCRIPTION/SUBSCRIBER word here is a PREFERENCE, not a gap in upstream's vocabulary, and RFC-0036 forbids resting a divergence on it. The RECEIVER half of the verdict is untouched and still holds: one session per image (RFC-0002) means the Executor owns the graph, and that is a real constraint.

HOW A USER FINDS OUT: COMPILE ERROR — unknown member — which is the good failure mode. The defect being recorded is in the RECORD, not in the user's experience: a reason a reviewer can falsify with one grep is the campaign's own "nothing validates a REASON", at the ledger. The same paragraph appears on `cpp:Node::`, `cpp:LifecycleNode::` and `rust:Executor::` variants of this key. Re-verified by hand against the current worktree before this row was written.

NO DISPOSITION IS WRITTEN on this row. The four dispositions are what clause 1 does to a CANDIDATE FROM CLAUSE 2 (RFC-0089), and this family's open question is a SPELLING — `subscription` here, `subscriber` upstream — and which one survives is the phase-417 stage-6 rename decision, not a constraint outcome. The RECEIVER half is a constraint and is already stated. See `cpp:Executor::get_subscription_names_and_types_by_node`.
